HeroSection.subtitle_3: to classify coins against 9,716 Corpus Nummorum types, validate material forensically, and generate a professional PDF report — typically in 15“60 seconds.

PipelineSteps.title: From photograph to report in four steps
PipelineSteps.desc: Every inference runs the full production pipeline — the same code that powers the live system, not a simplified demo path.
PipelineSteps.s1_desc: Drag-and-drop any coin photo. The engine auto-crops the coin region, applies CLAHE in LAB colour space, and resizes to 299 Ã— 299.
PipelineSteps.s2_desc: EfficientNet-B3 extracts a 1,536-dim feature vector. 8-pass Test-Time Augmentation averages softmax scores for 80.03 % TTA accuracy.
PipelineSteps.s3_desc: A LangGraph state machine routes by confidence. High: Historian (RAG + LLM). Mid: Validator (OpenCV forensics). Low: Investigator (VLM + BM25).
PipelineSteps.s4_desc: Synthesis agent assembles all outputs into a branded PDF — historical narrative, forensic material check, top-5 candidates, and KB attribution.

ValueCards.title: Built for production, not for demo
ValueCards.desc: Every engineering decision was driven by real constraints — limited VRAM, long-tail datasets, LLM hallucination risk, and archaeological accuracy requirements.
ValueCards.c1_desc: OpenCV HSV multi-scale analysis detects gold, silver, and bronze from the photograph itself — then cross-references with the knowledge base.
ValueCards.c2_desc: The Historian agent injects 5 labeled [CONTEXT N] blocks from ChromaDB into the Gemini prompt. The model may only cite what is in the context.
ValueCards.c3_desc: Below 40 % CNN confidence the Investigator agent uses VLM visual attributes + full KB search to surface the best match — never a blank response.
ValueCards.c3_b2: OpenCV fallback when no VLM key
ValueCards.c3_b3: Best visual match framing in UI

ForWhoCards.title: Who uses DeepCoin?
ForWhoCards.desc: Designed for everyone who works with ancient coins — from institutional conservators to weekend collectors.
ForWhoCards.c1_desc: Professional cataloguing in seconds. Attach the full-PDF report directly to collection management systems. Material validation prevents misattribution.
ForWhoCards.c2_desc: Query 9,716 Corpus Nummorum types through hybrid BM25 + vector search. Full citation trail — every fact is linked to a [CONTEXT N] source block.
ForWhoCards.c3_desc: Upload a photo from your phone. Get an instant estimate: denomination, mint, period, and metal — even for degraded specimens no algorithm has seen before.

Guide.step1_body: Navigate to the Analyse page and drag-and-drop any photo of an ancient coin onto the upload zone, or click to open the file picker.
Guide.step1_b2: Large images are auto-downsized to 1024 px before upload
Guide.step1_b3: Enable TTA (Test-Time Augmentation) for +0.78 % accuracy — takes ~5 s extra
Guide.step1_b4: Auto-crop detects the coin boundary and removes background noise
Guide.step1_b5: Requires a free account — sign up in seconds
Guide.step2_body: DeepCoin's EfficientNet-B3 model classifies your coin against 438 trained Corpus Nummorum types and routes it through a specialist agent.
Guide.step2_b1: 🟢 Identified — confidence >= 70 % — Historian agent writes a full narrative
Guide.step2_b2: 🔵 Consistent Match — 7 of 8 TTA passes agree — high visual consensus
Guide.step2_b3: 🟣 Deep Search — low confidence — Investigator searches all 9,541 KB types
Guide.step2_b4: Top-5 candidates link directly to corpus-nummorum.eu records
Guide.step3_body: The Explore page shows all past analyses from every user. Filter by AI route to find specific confidence tiers or coin families.
Guide.step3_b1: Filter by Historian / Validator / Investigator route
Guide.step3_b2: Click any card to view the full analysis with PDF download
Guide.step3_b3: CN type links open the official Corpus Nummorum record
Guide.step3_b4: No sign-in required — the gallery is fully public
Guide.step4_body: DeepCoin AI answers ancient coin questions grounded in 47,705 knowledge-base chunks covering 9,541 Corpus Nummorum types — not the open internet.
Guide.step4_b1: Ask about dynasties, mint cities, iconography, denominations, or dating
Guide.step4_b2: Every answer cites CN record IDs — all facts are verifiable
Guide.step4_b3: Paste a CN type ID from an analysis result for instant context
Guide.step4_b4: Google Search ↗ and Google Scholar ↗ buttons appear next to each answer for deeper academic research
Guide.step4_b5: Domain-specific only — it will not respond to off-topic questions
Guide.step5_body: Every analysis produces a professional PDF with a full historical narrative, forensic material check, visual attributes table, and a top-5 candidate matrix.
Guide.step5_b1: PDF links remain active for 30 days after analysis
Guide.step5_b2: Includes Corpus Nummorum references and mint/date attribution
Guide.step5_b3: Access past PDFs from the History page at any time
Guide.step5_b4: Reports are stored privately — only visible to you
Guide.step6_body: If the CNN misidentified a coin, use the 'Mark as wrong' button on the analysis panel to submit the correct CN type ID.
Guide.step6_b1: Your correction is logged in the active-learning feedback store
Guide.step6_b2: Admins review corrections in the admin panel
Guide.step6_b3: Repeated corrections on the same type trigger a retraining signal
Guide.step6_b4: Every expert correction makes the model better for everyone
Guide.intro_body: Follow the glowing dots to understand the pipeline.
